function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Sure! Building an AI “girlfriend” chatbot can be a fun project that lets you explore natural language processing, personality design, and conversational flow. Below is a step‑by‑step guide to help you get started, from choosing the right tools to deploying your bot. --- ## 1. Define the Purpose & Personality | Step | What to Decide | Why It Matters | |------|----------------|----------------| | **Goal** | Is it purely entertainment, companionship, or a learning tool? | Determines the tone, safety filters, and content scope. | | **Personality** | Friendly, supportive, witty, etc. | Sets the style of responses and helps maintain consistency. | | **Boundaries** | Topics to avoid (e.g., medical advice, personal data sharing). | Keeps interactions safe and respectful. | > **Tip:** Draft a short “personality profile” (e.g., “Alex is a 25‑year‑old music lover who loves deep conversations about art and science.”). This will guide the tone of all responses. --- ## 2. Choose Your Technology Stack | Option | Pros | Cons | |--------|------|------| | **OpenAI GPT‑4 / GPT‑3.5** | Powerful language generation, easy API integration. | Requires API key, usage costs. | | **Claude (Anthropic)** | Strong safety features, good for conversational bots. | Similar cost structure. | | **Local LLM (e.g., Llama 2, GPT‑NeoX)** | No API cost, full control over data. | Requires GPU resources, more setup. | | **Rasa + spaCy** | Open‑source, good for intent recognition and slot filling. | Needs more custom training. | > **Recommendation:** For beginners, start with the OpenAI API. It’s straightforward and has plenty of documentation. --- ## 3. Set Up the Development Environment 1. **Create a Project Folder** ```bash mkdir ai-girlfriend cd ai-girlfriend ``` 2. **Initialize a Virtual Environment** ```bash python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate ``` 3. **Install Dependencies** ```bash pip install openai flask python-dotenv ``` 4. **Store Your API Key Securely** Create a `.env` file: ``` OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx ``` Load it in your code: ```python from dotenv import load_dotenv import os load_dotenv() api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") ``` --- ## 4. Build a Simple Flask API ```python from flask import Flask, request, jsonify import openai import os from dotenv import load_dotenv load_dotenv() openai.api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") app = Flask(__name__) @app.route("/chat", methods=["POST"]) def chat(): data = request.json user_msg = data.get("message", "") # Build a prompt that includes personality context system_prompt = ( "You are Alex, a friendly and supportive AI girlfriend. " "You love music, art, and deep conversations. " "Respond in a warm, conversational tone." ) response = openai.ChatCompletion.create( model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}, {"role": "user", "content": user_msg} ], temperature=0.7, max_tokens=150 ) reply = response.choices[0].message.content.strip() return jsonify({"reply": reply}) if __name__ == "__main__": app.run(debug=True) ``` ### How It Works - **System Prompt**: Sets the overall persona and behavior. - **User Message**: The user’s input. - **Temperature**: Controls creativity (higher = more varied). - **Max Tokens**: Limits response length. --- ## 5. Add Safety & Moderation 1. **OpenAI Moderation API** ```python moderation = openai.Moderation.create(input=user_msg) if moderation.results[0].flagged: return jsonify({"reply": "Sorry, I can't respond to that."}) ``` 2. **Custom Filters** - Block profanity or disallowed content using regex or a library like `better_profanity`. - Enforce privacy rules (no personal data collection). --- ## 6. Deploy the Bot | Platform | Steps | |----------|-------| | **Heroku** | `git push heroku main`, set config vars (`OPENAI_API_KEY`). | | **Render** | Create a new web service, connect repo, set env vars. | | **AWS Lambda + API Gateway** | Package code, deploy via SAM or Serverless Framework. | | **Docker** | `docker build -t ai-girlfriend .`, run container. | > **Tip:** Use environment variables for secrets and keep your code in version control. --- ## 7. Front‑End Integration (Optional) If you want a web UI: ```html AI Girlfriend

Chat with Alex

``` Deploy this static page along with your Flask backend. --- ## 8. Iterate & Improve | Feature | How to Add | |---------|------------| | **Memory** | Store recent conversation history in a database or in‑memory cache. | | **Emotion Tracking** | Use sentiment analysis to adjust tone. | | **Voice Interaction** | Integrate TTS (e.g., Google Cloud Text‑to‑Speech) and STT (e.g., Whisper). | | **Learning** | Fine‑tune a smaller model on custom dialogues (requires dataset). | --- ## 9. Ethical Considerations - **Transparency**: Let users know they’re chatting with an AI. - **Consent**: Avoid collecting sensitive personal data without explicit consent. - **Safety**: Implement robust moderation to prevent harmful content. - **Respect**: Ensure the bot doesn’t reinforce stereotypes or biases. --- ## 10. Resources & Further Reading - **OpenAI Docs** – [Chat Completions](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/chat) - **Rasa** – [Open‑Source Conversational AI](https://rasa.com/) - **Hugging Face** – [Model Hub](https://huggingface.co/models) - **Python‑dotenv** – [Environment Variables](https://pypi.org/project/python-dotenv/) - **Flask** – [Micro‑framework for Python](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/) --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Define personality & boundaries - [ ] Pick a language model & platform - [ ] Set up environment & dependencies - [ ] Build a Flask API with system prompts - [ ] Add moderation & safety checks - [ ] Deploy (Heroku/Render/Docker) - [ ] Optional: Add a front‑end UI - [ ] Iterate based on user feedback Happy building! If you hit any snags or want deeper dives into specific parts (like fine‑tuning or adding voice), just let me know.
